subjects.introduction: Few teachings are harder to hear rightly than a warning of judgment, and few are easier to misuse. Bahá’u’lláh forbids the retaliation a wounded heart reaches for and prays forgiveness for those who wronged Him, yet He also speaks of a reckoning no one escapes: a deed returns upon the one who did it, while a whole people may suffer together, as a body does when one member carries a contagion. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá adds that this age belongs to favor more than to strict justice, and that a clean deed is never wasted. Fire and paradise, in this light, name nearness to God and separation from Him before they name any place, and the soul carries its condition beyond the grave. Ezekiel’s insistence that each soul answers for itself and may still turn back [1], the Qur’an’s pairing of justice with generous recompense [2], and the Dhammapada’s restraint born of noticing another’s pain [3] keep the inquiry honest. From here the road leads toward the justice and wrath of God, the law of cause and effect, and what awaits the spirit after death.
